events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded on the narrowest point: an account flag is a discretionary add-on (RD-6), and with 1 prior offence upheld in 90 days (F15) versus 2 disputes and 0 upheld for the rider (F14) I do not press flag_account. That concession does not touch RD-1/RD-2: the driver's good record cannot make 6.7 km of extra metered distance (F1, F7) authorised. [F15 F14 F1] [RD-6 RD-1]
→ D2: Correct that there is no chat at all (F8), and that is exactly why no segment is consented: RD-5 requires a rider message sent before the segment, and a rider who never messaged cannot be read as having authorised anything — silence is not the consent the clause demands. The absence of an objection in a record the rider had no reason to use does not convert an unauthorised route into an agreed one. [F8] [RD-5]
→ D3 (concedes): I accept F12 for the first segment: the 21:26 accident at 0 m from the optimal route, still listed in the trip window, is RD-4(a) corroboration and I concede F3. It is a single incident at a single point; it exempts the segment it replaced and nothing more, and F11's band 4 (30–39 km/h) adds only atmosphere since RD-4(b) says a band alone does not exempt. [F12 F11] [RD-4]
→ D4 (concedes): F3 is conceded as incident-exempt — but only 'for that segment' as RD-4(a) says; nothing in F12 or F8 extends the accident's reach to the second deviation, and RD-3 does not apply at all because no stop appears in the track and no rider message requested one (F8, F3). [F12 F3 F8] [RD-4 RD-3]
→ D5: F4 begins at 22:02, 36 minutes after the 21:26 report (F12), and D5's own premise is that traffic was still moving: KPE band 4 = 30–39 km/h (F11) and PIE band 5 = 40–49 km/h (F10) — neither band 1 nor band 2, so RD-4(b) gives no exemption and no incident record is tied to that window. Claiming 'same avoidance' for a 4.57 km loop that runs up to 997 m off the optimal route (F4) is an assertion, not a record, and it would extend a single 21:26 accident into a 43-minute exemption. [F4 F12 F11 F10] [RD-4 RD-1]
→ D6: F13 is neutral between us: fine weather removes a weather excuse but supplies no congestion excuse either, so it cannot carry D5's second segment, which still lacks any incident record. [F13] [RD-4]
→ D7: Agreed, and it cuts my way too: F9 is only a claim (and, with F8, also the only place consent or cause is asserted at all), so the judge must decide each segment on F3/F4 against F10–F12, not on the driver's wording. [F9 F8 F3 F4 F10 F11 F12] [RD-4 RD-5]
→ D8: Agreed on the method: refund base is only each unexempt segment's extra_km at this trip's rate $1.4101/km ($31.84 ÷ 22.58 km, F7), so F3's 2.69 km would be $3.79 and F4's 3.13 km is $4.41, and F5's $9.45 is the billed figure, not the refund base. Since I concede F3, my claim is $4.41 — that is exactly the amount I ask, so this point does not reduce it. [F7 F5 F3 F4] [RD-2]
→ D9: Agreed that no waiting fee ($0.00) and no surge (1.0×) are in dispute (F7, F6); my refund rests solely on the unexempt 22:02–22:09 segment, not on any FARE-1 add-on. [F7 F6] [FARE-1 RD-2]
Revised ask: refund_partial $4.41
